children: missed Wall Street estimates for third-quarter revenue and adjusted profit on Tuesday, as cautious spending by Chinese consumers amid an economic slowdown weighed on demand.
US-listed shares of the company, which have fallen about 4.04% so far this year through Monday's close, were down 3.41% in premarket trading.

JD.com is one of China's largest e-commerce groups and differentiates itself from marketplace-led rivals through a supply-chain-heavy model that includes direct retailing, warehousing and delivery operations
JD.com reported revenue of 309.6 billion yuan ($46.45 billion) for the third quarter, below analysts' average estimate of 311.48 billion yuan, according to data compiled by LSEG
Adjusted net profit came in at 8.3 billion yuan, below estimates of 8.59 billion yuan
Revenue from electronics and home appliances, its biggest product category, was 127.73 billion yuan, slightly above estimates of 127.44 billion yuan
A prolonged property downturn and job insecurity have prompted Chinese shoppers to prioritize value and discounts, while rising electronics prices continue to weigh on sales
JD.com faces heavy competition in e-commerce from Alibaba's Taobao and Tmall and PDD Holdings' Pinduoduo, which have all leaned on discounts and subsidies to win shoppers
